question: Who among the following had the shortest tenure as the President of India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Jawaharlal Nehru
Lal Bahadur Shastri
Zakir Husain
Rajendra Prasad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Zakir Husain

Explanation:
As the President of India, Zakir Husain had the shortest tenure. He assumed office on 13 May 1967 and served until his death on 3 May 1969, a period of just under 2 years. Rajendra Prasad served the longest tenure (about 12 years). Jawaharlal Nehru and Lal Bahadur Shastri were Prime Ministers, not Presidents. Zakir Husain was the third President and the first Muslim to hold the office.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ President with shortest tenure → Zakir Husain
☛ Zakir Husain's tenure → 13 May 1967 - 3 May 1969
☛ First Muslim President of India → Zakir Husain
☛ Zakir Husain awarded Padma Vibhushan → in 1954
☛ President with longest tenure → Rajendra Prasad
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसने भारत के राष्ट्रपति के रूप में सबसे कम समय तक कार्य किया? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)
options_hi: जवाहरलाल नेहरू
लाल बहादुर शास्त्री

Explanation:
भारत के राष्ट्रपति के रूप में ज़ाकिर हुसैन का कार्यकाल सबसे छोटा रहा। वे 13 मई 1967 को राष्ट्रपति बने और 3 मई 1969 को अपने निधन तक पद पर रहे, जो कि लगभग 2 वर्षों का था। इस प्रकार उनका कार्यकाल केवल 2 वर्ष से कम रहा। राजेंद्र प्रसाद ने सबसे लंबा कार्यकाल (लगभग 12 वर्ष) पूरा किया। जवाहरलाल नेहरू और लाल बहादुर शास्त्री प्रधानमंत्री थे, राष्ट्रपति नहीं। ज़ाकिर हुसैन तीसरे राष्ट्रपति थे और पहले मुस्लिम राष्ट्रपति भी थे।

question: Which of the following statements about the cardinal features of the political system in India are correct?1. It is a democratic republic.2. It has a Parliamentary form of government.3. The Supreme Power draws its power from the people of India.4. It provides for a unified authority.  (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Only 3 and 4
Only 1, 2 and 3
1, 2, 3 and 4
Only 1 and 2
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only 1, 2 and 3

Explanation:
The cardinal features of the Indian political system include: it is a democratic republic, where the people elect the government and the President is the head of state. India has a Parliamentary form of government, where the executive is responsible to the legislature. The supreme power is derived from the people of India, as mentioned in the Preamble. Statement 4 is incorrect because India does not provide for a unified authority; instead, it has a separation of powers and a federal structure, with the center and states functioning in their respective domains.

☛ Type of government → Parliamentary
☛ Source of power → People of India
☛ Nature of authority → Not unified, federal

question_hi: भारत की राजनीतिक व्यवस्था की मुख्य विशेषताओं के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन से कथन सही हैं?1. यह एक लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य है।2. इसमें संसदीय शासन प्रणाली है।3. सर्वोच्च शक्ति भारत के लोगों से अपनी शक्ति प्राप्त करती है।4. यह एक एकीकृत प्राधिकरण प्रदान करता है। (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)

1, 2, 3 और 4

Explanation:

question: Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution refers to _________. (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: right to equality
freedom of speech and expression
cultural educational rights
right against exploitation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is freedom of speech and expression

Explanation:
Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution grants citizens the freedom of speech and expression. It is a fundamental right under Part III and is considered the cornerstone of democracy. This right allows individuals to express their views through any medium—oral, written, print, or electronic. However, it is subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2), which include security of the state, foreign relations, public order, decency, and morality. This right is available only to citizens, not to foreigners. The Supreme Court has termed it as the 'bulwark of the temple of liberty'. The right also includes the freedom of the press and the right to information.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which Article deals with freedom of speech and expression? → Article 19(1)(a)
☛ Restrictions on Article 19(1)(a) are under which Article? → Article 19(2)
☛ Who is not entitled to freedom of speech? → Foreigners
☛ Part III of the Constitution deals with? → Fundamental Rights
☛ What did Supreme Court call freedom of speech? → Bulwark of the temple of liberty
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) _____________ को संदर्भित करता है। (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)
options_hi: समानता का अधिकार
वाक् स्वतंत्रता और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता
सांस्कृतिक शैक्षिक अधिकार
शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है वाक् स्वतंत्रता और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 19(1)(a) नागरिकों को वाक् स्वतंत्रता और अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता प्रदान करता है। यह मौलिक अधिकारों के अंतर्गत आता है और लोकतंत्र की आधारशिला माना जाता है। इस अधिकार के तहत व्यक्ति अपने विचारों को मौखिक, लिखित, प्रिंट, या किसी अन्य माध्यम से व्यक्त कर सकता है। हालांकि, यह अधिकार अनुच्छेद 19(2) के तहत उचित प्रतिबंधों के अधीन है, जिसमें राज्य की सुरक्षा, विदेशी संबंध, सार्वजनिक व्यवस्था, शालीनता और नैतिकता शामिल हैं। यह अधिकार केवल नागरिकों को उपलब्ध है, विदेशियों को नहीं। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने इसे 'स्वतंत्रता के मंदिर की आधारशिला' कहा है।

question: Which of the following constitutional bodies is responsible for ensuring Free and Fair Elections? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Election Commission of India
Parliament of India
Supreme Court of India
President of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Election Commission of India

Explanation:
The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body responsible for ensuring free and fair elections in the country. It was established on 25 January 1950 under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. The commission conducts elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, state legislative assemblies, and the offices of the President and Vice President. The Chief Election Commissioner and other commissioners are appointed by the President. The commission announces elections, enforces the Model Code of Conduct, and supervises the voting process. To ensure the Election Commission's independence, the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only through impeachment.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Constitutional provision for formation of Election Commission of India → Article 324
☛ Date of establishment of Election Commission of India → 25 January 1950
☛ Procedure to remove Chief Election Commissioner → Impeachment (by Parliament)
☛ Elections conducted by Election Commission of India → Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, Legislative Assemblies, President, Vice President
☛ Main function of Election Commission under Article 324 → Ensuring free and fair elections
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा संवैधानिक निकाय स्वतंत्र और निष्पक्ष चुनाव सुनिश्चित करने के लिए जिम्मेदार है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)

भारत का सर्वोच्च न्यायालय

Explanation:
भारत निर्वाचन आयोग एक संवैधानिक निकाय है जो देश में स्वतंत्र और निष्पक्ष चुनाव सुनिश्चित करने के लिए जिम्मेदार है। इसकी स्थापना 25 जनवरी 1950 को भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324 के तहत की गई थी। आयोग लोकसभा, राज्यसभा, राज्य विधानसभाओं और राष्ट्रपति एवं उपराष्ट्रपति के चुनावों का संचालन करता है। मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त और अन्य आयुक्तों की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है। आयोग चुनावों की घोषणा, आचार संहिता लागू करना और मतदान प्रक्रिया की निगरानी करता है। चुनाव आयोग की स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त को केवल महाभियोग प्रक्रिया द्वारा हटाया जा सकता है।

question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with the Fundamental Duties? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Part V A
Part VI A
Part III A
Part IV A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part IV A

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Part IV A of the Indian Constitution, which was added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976. Originally there were 10 duties; the 86th Amendment (2002) added one more duty (providing educational opportunities for children aged 6-14), making a total of 11 Fundamental Duties. These duties are covered under Article 51 A. They remind citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation, emphasizing respect for the Constitution, national symbols, and social harmony. This part is distinct from Fundamental Rights (Part III) and Directive Principles (Part IV).

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article dealing with Fundamental Duties → 51 A
☛ Amendment that added Fundamental Duties → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ Total number of Fundamental Duties → 11
☛ 86th Amendment related to → Right to education and one new duty
☛ Fundamental Duties inspired from → Constitution of Russia (USSR)
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा भाग मौलिक कर्तव्यों से संबंधित है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)

भाग VI A
भाग III A
भाग IV A

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में मौलिक कर्तव्यों का उल्लेख भाग IV A में किया गया है, जिसे 42वें संशोधन (1976) द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। मूल रूप से 10 कर्तव्यों को शामिल किया गया था, जिनमें से 86वें संशोधन (2002) द्वारा एक और कर्तव्य (6-14 वर्ष के बच्चों को शिक्षा के अवसर प्रदान करना) जोड़ा गया, जिससे कुल 11 मौलिक कर्तव्य हो गए। ये कर्तव्य अनुच्छेद 51 A के अंतर्गत आते हैं। मौलिक कर्तव्य नागरिकों को राष्ट्र के प्रति जिम्मेदारियों का स्मरण कराते हैं और संविधान, राष्ट्रीय प्रतीकों तथा सामाजिक सद्भाव का सम्मान करने पर बल देते हैं। यह भाग मौलिक अधिकारों (भाग III) और नीति निदेशक तत्वों (भाग IV) से भिन्न है।

question: What is the primary goal of fiscal consolidation? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Reducing Government debt
Stimulating economic growth
Increasing consumer expenditure
Reducing inflation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Reducing Government debt

Explanation:
The primary goal of fiscal consolidation is to reduce government debt and control the fiscal deficit. This is achieved through measures like cutting expenditure and increasing revenue. The aim is to ensure long-term economic stability and reduce the debt burden on future generations. Stimulating economic growth is not the primary goal, but it can be a positive outcome of a stable fiscal policy.

question_hi: राजकोषीय समेकन का प्राथमिक लक्ष्य क्या है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 2)

question: Who among the following holds office during the pleasure of the President? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Attorney General of India
Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Attorney General of India

Explanation:
According to Article 76 of the Indian Constitution, the Attorney General of India holds office during the pleasure of the President. This means the President can remove him at any time. This provision is different from other constitutional office holders. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha (Article 94) holds office until he becomes a member of the Lok Sabha or resigns. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (Article 148) can only be removed by the President through the process of impeachment. The Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (Article 316) can be removed by the President only on grounds of misbehaviour or incapacity, following the same procedure as removal of a High Court judge. Thus, only the Attorney General holds office at the pleasure of the President.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Holds office during pleasure of President → Attorney General of India
☛ Appointment of Attorney General → By President (Article 76)
☛ Term of Speaker of Lok Sabha → As long as he is a member of Lok Sabha
☛ Removal of CAG → Through impeachment (Article 148)
☛ Removal of UPSC Chairman → On grounds of misbehaviour/incapacity (Article 316)
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन राष्ट्रपति के प्रसादपर्यन्त पद धारण करता है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)

Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत का महान्यायवादी

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 76 के अनुसार, भारत का महान्यायवादी राष्ट्रपति के प्रसादपर्यन्त अपने पद पर रहता है। इसका अर्थ है कि राष्ट्रपति किसी भी समय उसे पद से हटा सकता है। यह प्रावधान अन्य संवैधानिक पदाधिकारियों से भिन्न है। लोकसभा अध्यक्ष (अनुच्छेद 94) पद धारण करता है जब तक वह लोकसभा का सदस्य है या त्यागपत्र न दे। भारत का नियंत्रक और महालेखा परीक्षक (अनुच्छेद 148) को राष्ट्रपति द्वारा महाभियोग की प्रक्रिया के माध्यम से ही हटाया जा सकता है। संघ लोक सेवा आयोग के अध्यक्ष (अनुच्छेद 316) को राष्ट्रपति द्वारा उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश को हटाने की प्रक्रिया के समान प्रक्रिया से ही हटाया जा सकता है। इस प्रकार, महान्यायवादी ही एकमात्र ऐसा पदाधिकारी है जो राष्ट्रपति के प्रसादपर्यन्त कार्य करता है।

question: Which of the following is the highest law officer in the Government of India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Judge of the Supreme Court
Attorney General of India
Chief Justice of India
Judge of High court
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Attorney General of India

Explanation:
The Constitution of India under Article 76 designates the Attorney General of India as the highest law officer of the Government of India. Appointed by the President, the Attorney General advises the government on legal matters, represents the government in the Supreme Court, and has the right to speak in both Houses of Parliament without the right to vote. He/she is also eligible to become the Chief Justice of India. In contrast, the Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary, not a law officer for the government, and the Judges of the Supreme Court or High Court are judicial officers, not law officers for the executive. Thus, only the Attorney General holds the title of the highest law officer.

question: Which of the following authorites in India have the power to terminate the citizenship of an individual under certain circumstances? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Union Government
Any State Government
Supreme Court
Delhi Government
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Union Government

Explanation:
In India, the power to terminate citizenship rests solely with the Union Government, as per Section 10 of the Citizenship Act, 1955. This power is exercised under specific circumstances such as fraud, false representation, or disloyalty to the country. State Governments, the Supreme Court, or the Delhi Government do not have this authority. Before issuing a termination order, the Union Government must provide the individual an opportunity of a hearing. Other grounds for termination include continuous residence abroad for five years or voluntarily acquiring citizenship of another country. The provision ensures that citizenship is revoked only after due process.

☛ Who else can terminate citizenship besides Union Government? → No one

question: Which Article of the Indian constitution deals with the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Article 145
Article 148
Article 142
Article 143
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 143

Explanation:
Article 143 of the Indian Constitution deals with the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court. Under this article, the President can seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact of public importance. The opinion given by the Supreme Court is not binding on the President. This provision enables the government to obtain legal clarity before a dispute arises. The Supreme Court's advisory opinion under Article 143 is not subject to judicial review. It is used to resolve important constitutional and legal questions. The Supreme Court, after hearing the matter, submits its report to the President.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution guarantees protection against arrest and detention in certain cases? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (03/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Article 22
Article 21
Article 23
Article 20
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 22

Explanation:
Article 22 of the Indian Constitution guarantees protection against arrest and detention in certain cases. This fundamental right applies when a person is arrested or detained, except in cases of anti-state activities. Article 22 grants the arrested person the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest, consult a lawyer, and be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours. It also provides safeguards in cases of preventive detention, though such laws are subject to certain limitations. Article 21 deals with right to life and personal liberty, while Article 20 provides protection against conviction for offences. Article 23 prohibits trafficking in human beings and forced labor.

question: What is the tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner of India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Six years
Five years or till the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier
Six years or till the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
At the pleasure of the President
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Six years or till the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier

Explanation:
The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India is six years or till the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. This provision is laid down under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution. The CEC is appointed by the President and enjoys the same security of tenure as a Judge of the Supreme Court. They can only be removed through impeachment. This independence ensures that the Election Commission functions impartially. The CEC's fixed tenure and high age limit protect them from political pressure, enabling free and fair elections in India.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states that it is the duty of every citizen of India to safeguard public property and to abjure violence? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 1)

The Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens are enshrined in Part IVA of the Constitution under Article 51A. These were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. This duty emphasizes the responsibility of citizens to protect national assets and promote non-violent behavior. question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for the Protection of ‘Life and Personal Liberty’? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Article 18
Article 25
Article 22
Article 21
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21

Explanation:
Article 21 of the Indian Constitution provides for the protection of 'Life and Personal Liberty'. It states that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. This Article is part of Part III (Fundamental Rights). The Supreme Court has termed it the 'heart' of the Constitution and the 'soul' of fundamental rights. The right to life under this Article is not merely about survival but includes the right to live with dignity. In the landmark case of Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India (1978), the Supreme Court gave a broad interpretation to this Article, linking it with Articles 14 and 19. Article 22 deals with protection against arrest and detention, Article 25 guarantees the right to religious freedom, and Article 18 abolishes titles.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provided power to the Supreme Court of India to review its own judgements?  (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Article 137
Article 140
Article 150
Article 138
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 137

Explanation:
Article 137 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgements. This power allows the court to reopen any judgement or order if there is an error or a mistake on the face of the record. The review petition is filed under the rules made under Article 145. This provision is a crucial part of judicial review, enabling the court to correct its own mistakes. Under Article 137, the Supreme Court can review its judgement in any case, whether civil, criminal, or constitutional. This provision is inspired by the American Constitution, where the Supreme Court has similar review powers. The review power is discretionary and is exercised only in exceptional circumstances to prevent a miscarriage of justice.

question: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for the post of the Chief Justice of India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 1)

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Has been for at least five years an advocate of a High Court or of two or more such Courts in succession

Explanation:
The criteria for appointment of the Chief Justice of India are laid down in Article 124(3) of the Constitution. question: Which of the following committees recommended the use of Mixed Reference Period against Uniform Reference Period? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Tendulkar Expert Group
NITI Aayog
National Sample Survey Organisation
C Rangrajan Committee
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tendulkar Expert Group

Explanation:
The Tendulkar Expert Group (2005) recommended the use of Mixed Reference Period (MRP) over Uniform Reference Period (URP) for measuring poverty. MRP uses a reference period of one year for durable goods and 30 days for non-durable goods, providing more accurate consumption estimates. The committee also revised the poverty line to ₹578 per capita per month in urban areas and ₹447 in rural areas (at 2004-05 prices). Additionally, it broadened poverty measurement by including requirements for food, education, and health. This recommendation was later implemented by the National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO). The Tendulkar methodology has been widely used in India for poverty estimation until recent updates.

solution:

Explanation:
In 2024, India introduced three new criminal laws: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA). These replace the colonial-era Indian Penal Code (IPC), Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), and Indian Evidence Act, respectively. The new laws came into effect on 1 July 2024. question: Which of the following was the strength of the Judges of Supreme Court of India after the commencement of the Constitution in 1950? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: 8
10
12
6
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 8

Explanation:
The Constitution of India came into effect on 26 January 1950. According to Article 124(1) of Part V, the Supreme Court consists of a Chief Justice and other judges. Initially, the total strength of judges was fixed at 8 (1 Chief Justice + 7 other judges). This number can be increased by law by Parliament. Subsequently, through various amendments, the number of judges has been increased. At present, the Supreme Court has 34 judges (1 Chief Justice + 33 other judges).

question: In which of the following years was the National Commission for Women established? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 2)
